history.heading: Ancient settlement
paragraphs: Papua New Guinea occupies the eastern half of the island of New Guinea and many smaller islands. People have lived there for at least 50,000 years. Highland communities developed agriculture independently around 7,000–10,000 years ago; the Kuk Early Agricultural Site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Austronesian peoples later settled coastal areas and islands.

history.heading: Colonial rule
paragraphs: In 1884 Germany claimed the northeast (German New Guinea) and Britain the southeast (British New Guinea). Australia took over British New Guinea, renamed Papua, in 1906, and seized German New Guinea in 1914. During the Second World War, fierce fighting took place, including along the Kokoda Track. Many Highland communities had no contact with outsiders until the 1930s.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Papua New Guinea became independent from Australia on 16 September 1975. A civil war on Bougainville, linked to a giant copper mine, lasted from 1988 to 1998 and killed thousands. In a 2019 referendum, 97.7 percent of Bougainvilleans voted for independence, which is still being negotiated with the national government.

culture.heading: Extraordinary diversity
paragraphs: Papua New Guinea is one of the most culturally diverse countries on Earth, with over 800 languages, about 12 percent of the world's total. Tok Pisin (a creole), English and Hiri Motu are official. Most people are Christian, often combined with traditional beliefs.

Communities are organised around clans, and the wantok system of mutual obligation is central. Sing-sings, festivals of dance and elaborate costumes such as the Goroka Show, are famous. Rugby league is the national passion.

politics.heading: Parliamentary democracy
paragraphs: Papua New Guinea is a parliamentary democracy and Commonwealth realm with the British monarch as head of state. Politics is fragmented, with many parties and independent MPs, and votes of no confidence are frequent. Tribal violence in the Highlands, crime and corruption are major issues. Australia is the main partner, and the two signed a mutual defence treaty in 2025.

economy.heading: Resource economy
paragraphs: Papua New Guinea is rich in natural resources: liquefied natural gas, gold, copper, nickel, oil, timber and palm oil. The PNG LNG project is the largest investment in the country's history. However, most of the population lives in rural areas and depends on subsistence farming, and infrastructure is limited.
